A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LSceneLLM work and contain complete, readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A-E. All 13 pages support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original LSceneLLM benchmark evaluations, ablations, attention visualizations, and computational-complexity results in Section 5 and Appendices B-E.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark results, ablations, qualitative analyses, and computational-complexity results reported in v1.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same coarse scene understanding module, dense vision token selector, scene magnifier, and adaptive self-attention. Their procedures and equations are unchanged.

E1.justification: Training and evaluation coverage is unchanged, including XR-Scene, XR-QA-S, ScanQA, other ScanNet tasks, and NuscenesQA. The additional tasks in Appendix C already appear in v1.

E2.justification: XR-Scene retains Chat-Scene, Leo, and Ll3da as comparators in Table 1. Comparator membership also matches in the other benchmark, module-integration, and computational-complexity comparisons.

E3.justification: Experimental settings and procedures are unchanged, including the 40k-point input, Llama2-7b backbone, evaluation metrics, baseline training arrangements, and ablation configurations.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same small-object and plug-and-play tests, token-selection ablations, attention visualizations, and computational-complexity analysis in Section 5 and Appendices B-E.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same point-estimate reporting. Neither introduces repeated-run counts, seed information, uncertainty intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1-11 and qualitative examples retain identical results. For example, LSceneLLM's XR-QA CIDEr remains 117.21 in Table 1, and ScanQA CIDEr remains 88.24 in Table 2.

T1.justification: The adaptive self-attention equations in Section 3.3 and their mathematical definitions are unchanged. No assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same claims about adaptive scene understanding, the XR-Scene benchmark, and improvements from the plug-and-play scene magnifier.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning detail loss, baseline behavior, token-selection tradeoffs, and computational scaling are unchanged. No new limitations, applicability boundaries, or failure conditions appear.

D1.justification: v2 adds an abstract statement directing readers to the Hoyyyaard/LSceneLLM GitHub repository for code and data; v1 lacks this statement. Existing implementation details are unchanged. The PDFs alone do not establish repository accessibility or completeness.

R1.justification: Section 2 and all 48 references are unchanged. The positioning relative to object-centric approaches and LL3DA retains the same meaning.

P1.justification: v2 adds the code-and-data access sentence to the abstract and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. Otherwise, the prose and section organization match after accounting for text reflow.

P2.justification: The longer abstract moves the Introduction opening to the right column and reflows pages 1-4, including tighter equation spacing. Figures and tables retain their content and numbering; pages 5-13 render identically.

improvement.justification: The repository pointer supplies previously missing code-and-data access information, modestly improving reproducibility guidance. Scientific content and supporting evidence remain unchanged, so the benefit is limited to documentation; repository contents are unverified.
